title: SAS utils
description: Shared sub-schemas reused by every SAS per-type document (mosfet, diode, igbt, bjt). Component-specific electricals, modelParams and curves live in the per-type files.

part.title: semiconductorPart
part.description: Part identification — shared across all semiconductor types. Extends the PEAS datasheetInfoPartBase with semiconductor-specific fields.

subType.description: Per-device-type subtype. The legal values are NARROWED BY EACH DEVICE SCHEMA (mosfet/diode/igbt/bjt.json) to a closed enum; this shared def only fixes the type. Optional: omit when unknown.

package.description: Manufacturer's exact package designation (e.g. Infineon PG-TDSON-8). Complements case, which holds the generic industry code.

dieConfiguration.title: dieConfiguration
dieConfiguration.description: How many die the package holds and how their channels relate. Absent means the package holds one die, which is the overwhelming majority; state it explicitly only when the datasheet does. 'dual' = two die of the SAME channel type (onsemi SO-8FL Dual, Infineon Dual SSO8, TI two-FET power blocks); 'complementary' = one n-channel and one p-channel die in one package (YAGEO XP6C..., Vishay Si...DS). A part declaring 'dual' or 'complementary' MUST carry per-die data and MUST NOT carry a package-level electrical block — see mosfet.json.

internalConnection.title: dieInternalConnection
internalConnection.description: How the die are wired to each other INSIDE the package, when the datasheet says so. 'independent' = no internal connection between the die; 'commonDrain' / 'commonSource' = the stated terminals are bonded internally (YAGEO prints 'Common-Drain' in its own Configuration column); 'halfBridge' = the drain of one die is bonded to the source of the other, forming a switching node (Infineon 'Dual SSO8 HB', TI power blocks). Omit when the datasheet does not state the internal arrangement — do not infer it from the package or the part number.

dieBase.title: semiconductorDieBase
dieBase.description: Identity of ONE die inside a multi-die package, shared by the device schemas. Device files extend it with their own electrical/thermal blocks and seal the result with unevaluatedProperties: false (the RAS pattern); this base is deliberately unsealed so it can be extended.

name.description: The datasheet's own label for this die — 'Q1', 'Q2', 'Channel 1'. Unique within the part. Taken verbatim and never invented: a datasheet that does not distinguish its die gives no die entries to write.

role.description: The datasheet's functional name for the die where it gives one ('Control FET', 'Sync FET', 'High-Side'), verbatim. Free text because vendors do not share a vocabulary; it is a label, never a substitute for the electrical data.

pins.description: Pin identifiers belonging to this die, matching entries of mechanical.pinout, so a circuit can bind to one die rather than to the package. Note what the schema cannot check: that the pinout contains these ids, that no pin is claimed by two die, and that die names are unique — those are the ingest gate's job, exactly as for CIAS component URIs.

mechanical.title: semiconductorMechanical
mechanical.description: Mechanical specs — extends PEAS datasheetInfoMechanical with a package case field.

case.description: Package name (TO-220, SOT-23, etc.) — mirrors part.case for convenience.

pinout.description: Per-terminal function map (shared PEAS type, hoisted 2026-08): (pin, name, function) triples — e.g. G/D/S plus kelvinSource on 4-lead packages. Same package does NOT imply same pinout (pin-swapped second sources exist).

landPattern.description: Manufacturer-recommended PCB land pattern (shared PEAS type, hoisted 2026-08): pad centres, copper sizes and drills exactly as the datasheet's recommended-layout drawing publishes them.

spiceModel.title: spiceModel
spiceModel.description: The device's SPICE .model card, carried as structured data for simulator-agnostic round-trip (ngspice and LTspice consume .model cards identically). This is the canonical home for a device whose source is a simulation model rather than a datasheet — it lives at the device-body top level so it does not require the manufacturerInfo/datasheetInfo chain. Nothing is fabricated: a bare card such as '.model Red D' yields modelType 'D' and an empty parameters object.

modelName.description: Model name exactly as it appears in the .model card (e.g. '1N4148', 'Red').

modelType.description: SPICE model type keyword following the name in a .model card (e.g. 'D' for diode, 'NPN'/'PNP' for BJT, 'VDMOS'/'NMOS'/'PMOS' for MOSFET, 'NIGBT' for IGBT).

parameters.description: SPICE .model parameters as name -> value, SI-resolved (numbers, or strings for non-numeric flags). Empty object when the card carries only type defaults.
